TITLE: ABB Q3 2026: record orders, but the premium needs broader growth

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Orders rose 40% to a record USD 12.1bn, 8% above consensus, led by data centres.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Miss
TAKEAWAYS.text: Basic EPS of USD 0.65 missed consensus by about 17%, partly on a USD 115m non-cash hedge charge.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: Growth is narrow: Automation orders were flat at USD 2.1bn, 9% below consensus.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: At 25.6x consensus earnings, 36% above the 2006 to 2026 average, the shares need upgrades.

H_P1: The case now rests on electrification
P1_PARAGRAPH: ABB is becoming an electrification company with an industrial tail. Electrification orders rose 70% on a comparable basis to USD 7.7bn and its order book reached a record USD 16bn, up 83% on the year, which secures growth into 2027 and 2028. Elsewhere momentum is thinner: Motion grew orders 12% but lost one percentage point of margin, and Automation orders were flat. The shares fell 5.5% on the day because investors had already paid for the strong part.
C1_SUB: Reported vs. pre-results consensus, % · EPS vs. the midpoint of USD 0.77 to 0.79 · operational EBITA and segment surprises approximate
C1_COMMENT: The lines that point to future earnings beat; the line that prices the stock today missed. Orders and free cash flow, 29% above consensus, show strong demand and cash conversion. The USD 115m revaluation of a currency hedge linked to the Rotork acquisition is non-cash and explains about half of the EPS shortfall. The rest, and the 9% gap in Automation orders, are real.
BASE_CASE: We stay constructive on ABB and hold, but would not add at current levels. We underwrite full-year revenue growth in the low teens and an operational EBITA margin up at least 270 basis points, knowing that about CHF 240m of Q4 property gains flatter it. Demand is not the debate any more; breadth and conversion are: can the USD 16bn Electrification backlog lift 2027 earnings while Automation and Motion lag? The catalyst would be 2027 upgrades, and consensus 2026 EPS has risen only 1% since the July results. With the shares 7% below their 40-week average, sentiment has reset. The next test is the Q4 release in early 2027.
UPSIDE: Q4 orders hold above USD 11bn with Electrification orders still well ahead of revenues; Automation orders return to growth as delayed large projects are booked; consensus 2027 EPS rises 5% or more before the Q4 results.
DOWNSIDE: Data centre customers push out deliveries despite their deposits; the Electrification margin slips below 24% as large projects ramp up; the Q4 margin is flat only thanks to property gains; weakness in the Middle East spreads to other regions.
H_A1: Results: the beat was in orders, not earnings
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Electrification carried the quarter. Orders rose 70% organically to USD 7.7bn, about 16% above consensus, with triple-digit growth in data centres and a 117% jump in the Americas; utilities, semiconductors and grid infrastructure also contributed. Revenues increased 21% to USD 5.4bn and operational EBITA 27% to USD 1.4bn, a 25.6% margin. On the call, management addressed the durability question directly: data centre orders are secured by large down payments and clear cancellation clauses, and each contract is tied to a specific site with permits and grid connections, which limits the risk of withdrawal. The 800-volt direct current Infinitus portfolio, with a solid-state transformer due in the second half of 2027, should support mix.

The rest of the group was weaker. Motion orders grew 12% organically, but its margin fell 100 basis points to 19.1%, partly due to the newly acquired Gamesa Electric. Automation orders were flat at USD 2.1bn, with the margin up 90 basis points to 14.8%; management attributes the sequential slowdown to the timing of large projects, but the Middle East has been subdued since Q1. At group level, gross margin fell 60 basis points to 40.6% on unrealised FX and commodity derivative effects, and pricing of just over 2% only offset cost inflation. Free cash flow of USD 1.58bn cut net debt to 0.2x EBITDA.
H_A2: Outlook: a softer Q4 and a new Japan platform
A2_PARAGRAPH: Guidance rose less than orders. ABB expects full-year revenue growth in the low teens and an operational EBITA margin up at least 270 basis points, including about CHF 240m of Q4 property gains, so the underlying upgrade is modest. For Q4, management guides to low to mid single-digit revenue growth and a broadly stable margin. Robotics should be sold by late 2026 and Rotork closes by mid-2027. ABB will pay USD 495m for 51% of a joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric’s low-voltage business, valued at about EUR 890m on EUR 640m of revenue: a Japanese market leader targeting a margin of at least 20% within five years.
H_C2: Valuation: the premium waits for 2027 upgrades
C2_TITLE: ABBN: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: Weekly, Jan 2006 to 20 Oct 2026, resampled from daily · Bloomberg BEst EPS for the current fiscal year in USD (steps each January) vs. price in CHF and its 40-week MA · log scales · P/E vs. its 2006 to 2026 average · last price is the 20 October close, after the release
C2_COMMENT: The price has run with earnings, not ahead of them, but the multiple is still rich. The shares are up 21% over 12 months and 20% this year, while consensus 2026 EPS has risen 15% since January. Since the July results, however, the price has fallen 10% and EPS has risen only 1%. The P/E of 25.6x is 36% above its 18.8x average since 2006, down from a 33.2x peak on 3 July 2026 and a one-year average of 28.9x. A 10% upgrade at an unchanged price would take the multiple to 23.3x, still 24% above the average.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, analyst research notes of 20 October 2026
